hero.title: Build Scalable Microservices
hero.subtitle: A specification-driven development methodology that enables scalable, large-scale microservice systems without architectural degradation. Let AI handle the implementation while you focus on business logic.

overview.title: Overview of the Method
overview.description: I have designed an innovative development method that leverages artificial intelligence to implement software systems based on precise, evolving specifications. Conceptually, this approach is a refined form of spec-driven development, adapted specifically for AI-assisted coding.
overview.highlight: Unlike ad-hoc prompt-based or "vibe coding" approaches, development in this method strictly follows structured documentation. All technical details are progressively generated, expanded, and maintained by AI, while remaining fully transparent and editable for the development team at every stage. An end-to-end sample microservice application (with GitHub source code) has been built using this method and is available for inspection.

coreComponents.title: Core Components
coreComponents.subtitle: The method consists of two fundamental phases

useCase.title: Use Case Definition
useCase.description: Use cases are generated with AI assistance and reviewed, edited, or authored by humans as needed. These use cases define the business logic, constraints, and expected behavior of the system.

implementation.title: AI-Driven Implementation
implementation.description: Each approved use case is converted into back-end and front-end code entirely by AI, guided by the accumulated documentation and predefined architectural constraints.

coreComponents.note: Use cases are not required upfront. Development proceeds incrementally: each new use case extends the codebase and documentation in a controlled and consistent manner.

roles.title: Human vs AI Roles
roles.subtitle: This method follows a clear human-in-the-loop model
roles.note: Documentation acts as the contract between human intent and AI execution. The development team does not write code directly.

authoring.title: Authoring and Reviewing Use Cases
authoring.description: The team reviews and refines AI-generated use cases or authors them from scratch when domain knowledge is required. The quality of use cases directly determines the quality of the resulting system. For example, in the sample microservice application presented at the end, all use cases in the list below are implemented by AI. Also an example of a complete use case is provided.

architecture.title: Selecting Architecture and Technology
architecture.description: Architectural patterns, technology stacks, and constraints are selected by the team and recorded in predefined prompts. These decisions guide all subsequent AI-generated output.
architecture.note: All process documentation is automatically produced and maintained by AI; the team does not manually manage documentation artifacts.

solution.title: This method addresses these issues through:
items: Incremental scope expansion per use case

problems.result: As a result, AI retains an effective understanding of the system regardless of project size.

items.title: Reduced Cost
items.description: Reduced engineering cost by removing manual coding

items.title: Easy Onboarding
items.description: Reduced onboarding complexity for new developers

items.title: Consistent Quality
items.description: Consistent architecture and UI/UX across large codebases

applicability.title: Applicability and Scope
applicability.description: This method imposes no limitations on programming language, framework, architecture, or application size. It can be applied in any IDE connected to an AI assistant. The sample project was implemented using VS Code and GitHub Copilot, but the approach is tool-agnostic.
applicability.migration: Existing projects can adopt this method provided their documentation is restructured according to the defined schema. While this migration requires effort, it is feasible.
